filename: Dryland evapotranspiration from remote sensing solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence_ Constraining an optimal stomatal model within a two-source energy balance model.pdf
title: Dryland evapotranspiration from remote sensing solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence: Constraining an optimal stomatal model within a two-source energy balance model
code_availability: Data and Gc-TSEB code will be made available on request.
testbed_rationale: The study develops a semi-mechanistic physical land-surface model (Gc-TSEB) calibrated with MCMC rather than training an ML parameterization, and model code is available only on request.
pain_points: Spatial scale mismatch between 0.05-degree remote sensing SIF pixels and sub-kilometer eddy covariance tower footprints
High sub-pixel landscape heterogeneity in drylands and tree-grass savanna ecosystems
Decoupling of the SIF-photosynthesis relationship under intense water stress, drought, and heatwaves
Lack of reliable, high-resolution root-zone soil water content estimates to constrain stomatal regulation
Errors in satellite land surface temperature retrievals used for model calibration
extraction_notes: The study focuses on physically based and semi-mechanistic modelling (Two-Source Energy Balance model coupled with Medlyn optimal stomatal conductance model), using MCMC for parameter calibration. ML is involved upstream in the creation of the CSIF input product (Zhang et al. 2018a), but no new ML architecture is developed in this work.
